3.r: Obama family [accept Barack Obama or Hussein Obama or Stanley Ann Obama] (The memoir is Dreams From my Father.)

3.q: This politician has been repeatedly forced to defend his referring to members of Hamas as "friends." This politician's idea of using quantitative easing to fund infrastructure is called "People's QE." He has proposed the (*) re-nationalization of major industries like coal and steel, a throwback to the pre-Thatcher era. Ed Miliband was replaced by - for 10 points - what recently elected far-left leader of the British Labour Party?

The leader of one of these organizations caused outrage by distributing 59 free Hummers to members. One of these organizations led by Tom Vogel endorsed Tom Torlakson in a runoff against Marshall Tuck. Elba Esther Gordillo, the leader of one of these organizations called the NSTE, was arrested in September 2013 in Mexico. An alleged brain tumor has prevented a leader of one of these organizations from challenging (*) Rahm Emanuel for mayor in Chicago. Two of these groups joined California in defense of a "last-in, first-out" law in the case Vergara v. California. These organizations, such as ones led by Karen Lewis and Randi Weingarten, consistently oppose merit pay systems like those introduced by Michelle Rhee. For 10 points, name these organizations which, in the United States, include the AFT and the National Education Association.
3.r: teachers’ unions [prompt on “unions” or “public-sector unions” or “government worker unions” or anything less specific]

3.q: This resource is mined in the Scottish village of Lochaline, which was visited by Ed Conway in the first of six parts of a 2023 book. Chinese vessels have attempted to covertly collect this resource from Taiwan's Matsu Islands. India has violent "mafias" that illegally export this resource, whose mining has endangered gharials and Lake Poyang's freshwater porpoises. Environmentalists have decried Indonesia's massive exports to this resource's largest importer, (*) Singapore. New Jersey has spent billions on "nourishment" projects that have replenished this resource after a 2012 natural disaster. A U.S. admiral claimed that China was making a "Great Wall" of this resource in the South China Sea as part of its reclamation process. This substance is dredged to manufacture concrete. For 10 points, name this silica-rich substance collected from beaches.
3.r: sand [or gravel; accept silica until mentioned; accept sand mafias or the “Great Wall of Sand”; prompt on land or sediment] (The Ed Conway book is Material World: The Six Raw Materials That Shape Modern Civilization. New Jersey is spending billions on beach nourishment after Hurricane Sandy.)

3.q: A study by the University of Minnesota about this project counted 25 trillion of its so-called "persistent word views" and found that nearly half of those PWVs was attributed to less than 0.1% of all possible sources. A 10th anniversary survey of this project showed that barely 10% of its population was female, which worried CEO Sue Gardner of the (*) Foundation that runs it. The 2007 development of a namesake scanner for this project allowed tracing of anonymous changes made to this project to institutions like Congress and the CIA, a link that could determine violations of its Neutral Point of View policy. For 10 points, name this free, online encyclopedia.

Vermont's governor recently proposed funding one of these programs by shifting money from the earned income tax credit. David Weikart developed the HighScope Approach used in these programs in Michigan, where they were the subject of the Perry study. The Frank Porter Graham Institute concluded that these policies could be effective in an experiment conducted in North Carolina, the (*) Abecedarian Project. In the 2013 State of the Union, Barack Obama claimed "every dollar" spent on these programs will save "seven dollars" in the future. The Race to the Top Early Challenge funds these programs. For 10 points, name this type of program implemented nationally under Head Start, which provides education to children under five years old.
3.c: 2013 Western Invitational Tournament Pkt UVA Q6

3.q: The first male Londoner to carry an umbrella, Jonas Hanway, published a four hundred page diatribe against this resource for being a threat to English masculinity. Erika Rappaport's 2018 history on how this resource "shaped the modern world" describes how the English had a single name for it prior to the publication of clergyman John Ovington's Voyage to Surat in 1689. Smugglers from the notorious Hawkhurst gang quilted this resource under their coats to avoid detection. The Scotsman Robert (*) Fortune infamously stole the source of this good while employed by the British East India Company. After purchasing this good on credit in Canton, British merchants would balance their debts by selling opium and smuggling it back to China. Nearly every word for this good worldwide falls into one of three different groups, all of which trace back to Chinese. For 10 points, name this good, crates of which were destroyed in 1773 in Boston Harbor.
3.c: 2019 Chicago Open Pkt 08 Gupta + Vardomskaya Q8

3.q: Prohibiting this industry from using LOGINK, a Chinese data management software, is one provision of a bill by Mark Kelly and Todd Young targeting this industry. Negotiations over a labour dispute in this industry were stalled after an automated gate system was discovered in Mobile, Alabama. An incident involving this industry was responsible for the partial destruction of a landmark named for (*) Francis Scott Key in Baltimore. Harold Daggett was involved in the negotiation of a 62% wage hike for certain workers in this industry between the USMX and the ILA following an October 2024 strike. An Egyptian state-owned company demanded $916 million in compensation for a crisis that forced this industry to rely on the Cape Route around South Africa. For 10 points, name this industry in which the Ever Given caused disruption by blocking the Suez Canal.
3.r: shipping [accept maritime industry; accept cargo industry; accept freight industry; accept ports; accept harbors; accept dockworking; prompt on transport; prompt on logistics]

3.q: A group in this country executed Swiss missionary Beatrice Stockli about a year after massacring 100 Christians in the town of Sobame Da. The librarian Abdul Kader led an operation in this country in which thousands of subversive medieval manuscripts were smuggled out of an embattled city by donkey cart. A battle in this country's town of Talahandak killed JNIM affiliate and (*) Al-Qaeda leader Abdelmalek Droukdel. ECOWAS has applied sanctions to this country since Assimi Goita and Bah Ndaw took power shortly before its previous leader went to the UAE for medical treatment. The Tuareg sepertist MNLA based in the north of this country have called for the re-establishment of the Azawad state. An August 2020 coup ousted Ibrahim Boubacar Keita as the president of, for 10 points, what West African country where the Islamist group Ansar Dine have carried out attacks in Timbuktu?
3.r: Republic of Mali [prompt on Azawad until “Azawad” is read]

3.q: David Elms, the founder of a review site for this industry, was arrested in 2009 for attempting to arrange a hit. A study by SUNY sociologist Angela Jones describes how this industry institutionalizes white supremacy with the example of Sunny Olivia, who in August 2015 wore an SS uniform and displayed a Nazi flag. The 2009 film Middle Men dramatizes how e-commerce was effectively pioneered by this industry. A companion term to (*) "TERF'' describes a form of radical feminism that excludes the perspectives of these workers. Citing pressure from banks like JPMorgan Chase, a London-based company announced but soon reversed an August 2021 decision to effectively ban performers in this industry, many of whom organized in protest of the passage of FOSTA-SESTA. For 10 points, name this industry whose workers host content on the subscription service OnlyFans.

Anthropologist Susan Bronwell's 1995 book on sports in this country examined crazes like "old people's disco dancing" and introduced the term "body culture." In 2017, officials in this country mandated that every top-tier soccer team field an under-23 player, but the rule had to be modified after many teams substituted out the player in under a minute. A June 2021 article in the New Yorker related Peter Hessler's attempt to learn to ski at newly built slopes in this country. A burgeoning sportswear brand in this country, (*) Anta, makes shoes branded for Klay Thompson. This country's government imposed a ban on all extreme sports following a 2021 ultramarathon where plummeting temperatures left 21 racers dead. Young eSports athletes in this country were hurt by a 2021 law limiting gaming hours for minors to 3 hours a week. For 10 points, name this country which will host the 2022 Winter Olympics.

When running for re-election, this politician chose Mar'ruf Amin as their running mate in order to defiect claims that they are "insuficiently Muslim and too pro-minority". In contrast to the grandiose names chosen for previous Cabinets, this politician named their first government the "Working Cabinet". In their first elected position, this politician was known for introducing the concept of blusukan, impromptu visits to investigate local administration. Born in Solo, this politician started out as a furniture maker, contrasting with the elite background of the man they defeated in their most recent election, (*) Prabowo Subianto. This world leader hosted the G20 in November 2022, where they promoted their planned new capital, Nusantara. Previously Governor of Jakarta, for 10 points, name this current President of Indonesia.
3.r: Joko Widodo [accept Jokowi ; prompt on Widodo (it is not a surname, but we are being generous in allowing a prompt since some Western sources use it alone)]

3.q: A now disabled Twitter account called "HSM Press Office" controversially tweeted that this country was experiencing "largely miniscule...retributive justice." After an electric transformer exploded in this country in 2015, a stampede broke out and several young people jumped from windows. The U.S. State Department and Major Emmanuel Chirchir questioned a NYPD report about events in this country that suggested that fugitives were still on the loose and not dead. The hashtag #147notjustanumber (*) (not-just-a-number) trended as result of events here, which resulted in nightly curfews imposed in Wajir and the Tana River counties. The government of this country put a million dollar bounty on former school teacher and principal Mohamed Kuno. This country's Garissa University College was the site of a targeted attack on Christian students. For 10 points, name this country where Al-Shabaab gunmen killed 147 people in April of 2015.
3.c: 2015 Chicago Open Pkt 11 - Theoretical Expenditures of the Leisure Class Q10

3.q: A flier featuring the snarling face of this politician claims "you did nothing" in orange text on a black background, characteristic of a non-profit whose name means "No to [this person]." This politician's brother accepted bribes to vote against removing the president, according to videos leaked by Moises Mamani ("moy-SACE mah-MAH-nee"). This politician led efforts to impeach Pedro Pablo Kuczynski ("koo-CHEEN-skee"), or PPK. In May 2020, this politician bailed out of three years of pretrial detention for allegedly receiving money from (*) Odebrecht ("oh-deh-BRESH"), as revealed by a neighboring country's Operation Car Wash. This leader of the Popular Force narrowly lost elections in 2011, 2016, and 2021, most recently to the former teacher Pedro Castillo ("kah-STEE-yoh"). This woman acted as First Lady during the tenure of her father in the 1990s. For 10 points, name this Peruvian politician of Japanese descent.

This group was responsible for a brief 136 billion dollar stock drop in April 2013 when it planted a story about a fictitious bombing of the White House. This group first emerged in July 2011, when member "The Pro" targeted UCLA. This group was responsible for allegations that a Saudi weather station had gone down due to a head on-collision with a (*) camel and for an October 2013 attack on the Gmail account of Organizing for Action, which enabled the manipulation of the URL service Shortswitch and thus the redirecting of links posted on Barack Obama's Twitter to a graphic twenty-four minute propaganda video on Youtube. For 10 points, name this hacking group whose usual methodology is to hijack Twitter accounts and denounce enemies of Bashar al-Assad.

In a book by Robert Bevan, the ideology of the perpetrators of this event is said to derive from Heidegger's belief of a "rootedness in native soil." This event resulted in the discovery of fifty caves, inside of which are the world's oldest-known oil paintings that have survived. This event partly centered on an object called "Solsol" whose name, meaning "year after year," bore symbolic importance for the thirteen prisoners of war who were (*) dangled on ropes and forced to carry it out. This event was the culmination of a campaign that included therazing of the city of Yakawlang ("YAHK-ow-long"), intended to break the culture of the Hazara peoples. It ostensibly took place after a group of Swedish scholars offered to restore the heads of two works in the Gandhara style, angering Mullah Omar. For 10 points, what action, carried out in 2001 by the Taliban, blew up some large religious statues?
3.r: destruction of the Bamiyan Buddhas [accept any reasonable answer which indicates blowing up the Buddha statues in Bamiyan Valley; prompt on destruction of Buddhas by asking “please name the valley where the Buddhas were found”]

3.q: In 2019 this country's president was given the highest award of the International Cycling Union for this country's dedication to the sport, and the 2021 track cycling world championships will be held there. The President of this country, who showed off by lifting a gold-plated weightlifting bar in a cabinet meeting, ended decades of free gas and electricity for citizens in 2018 . This country's president has claimed that it has had zero (*) cases of COVID, and that licorice may be a cure for the disease. The same month, a 6m tall golden statue of an Alabay, a breed of dog native to this country, was unveiled by this country's president, Gurbanguly Berdymukhamedov. For 10 points, name this central Asian country known for its repressive government, which meets in Ashgabat.

One campaign billboard for this man showed him in front of a pile of vegetables criticizing rising onion prices. In October 2013, multiple bombs exploded at a Hunkar campaign rally led by this man in the city of Patna. This man claimed that his country's ancestors played with snakes, but now play with a mouse in a September 2014 speech. He was accused of being complicit in Ehsan Jafri's death after a fire on a train led to the Gulbarg Society massacre and spent time as a campaigner for the (*) RSS. His supporters handed out paper cups with his picture on it to celebrate his background as a tea seller as he stood for Vadodara constituency in a 2014 election using many saffron-colored campaign posters to attack the Congress Party. For 10 points, identify this former Chief Minister of Gujarat, a member of the BJP who defeated Rahul Gandhi to become Prime Minister of India.

In June 2023, this country announced plans to complete a debt-to-nature swap for investments in Cabo Verde's environmental and climate fund. The H2Sines project located in this country aims to export green hydrogen produced from water electrolysis. In April 2021, this country cited a failed environmental impact study to cancel plans to develop a mine in a traditional farming region near this country's (*) Peneda-Geres ("zheh-RAYSH") National Park. One project by Savannah Resources in this country expected to finish by 2025 would become the first European mine to produce battery-grade lithium. In November 2023, this country's Prime Minister resigned amidst allegations of illicit concessions provided to various environmental projects. For 10 points, name this country formerly led by Antonio Costa.

In February 2025, this company's CEO and a telecom CEO were conspicuously placed directly across from a national leader during a pro-business rally in the Great Hall of the People. This company's CEO met directly with Lula after slave-like conditions were reported at its factory construction site in Bahia. This company's subsidiary, FinDreams, competes directly with CATL. This is the largest national producer of a product category that the Biden administration blocked from the US market with (*) 100 percent tariffs. Wang Chuanfu quickly grew this company in Shenzhen by cheaply manufacturing lithium-ion batteries for cell phones, before it entered its main sector with models like the Qin and Seagull. For 10 points, what Chinese auto company is the world's largest manufacturer of electric cars?
3.r: BYD Company Limited [or BYD Autos; accept Build Your Dreams; accept Bǐyàdí]

3.q: The Cathcart Report advocated creating this organization. The 1956 Guillebaud Report found that this organization was not wasting money. PCTs in this system are required to break even at the end of each year. This system adopted a tripartite structure in a deal mediated by Aneurin (*) Bevan; Bevan ultimately resigned when it started charging for certain services. The creation of this organization was deemed necessary to provide for social security in the Beveridge Report. Fund holders in this system were attacked by Tony Blair's government. For 10 points, name this entity that provides medical care to Britons.

An innovation in these devices was first employed by the "New Year's Gang" of students in Madison, Wisconsin. In 1927, Andrew Kehoe committed suicide using one of these devices in Bath Township, Michigan after losing a municipal election. A 2017 book about the impact of these devices covers their use in "festivals of plastic" by the OAS. A "brief history" of these devices by Mike Davis is named after one of them that was employed by Mario (*) Buda. The Cedar Revolution was launched after Rafic Hariri was killed by one of these devices, and one of these devices consisting of ammonium nitrate fertilizer was used in Ramzi Yousef's attack on the World Trade Center. For 10 points, name these devices often employed in terrorist attacks that consist of an IED attached to a motor vehicle.
3.r: car bombs [or truck bombs; or bus bombs; or vehicle-borne improvised explosive devices; or VBIEDs; prompt on bombs or improvised explosive devices or IEDs; prompt on suicide bombs before “suicide” is given]

3.q: The Soviet propaganda film Why did I do that? concerned this practice. In another country, decretsei were created due to a ban on this practice. In that country, Decree 770 banned this practice. One Holocaust survivor sarcastically apologized for being a woman addressing an all-male assembly before a speech defending this practice. This practice was legalized in the USSR in 1920, banned in 1936, and re-legalized in 1956. The death of Savita (*) Halappanavar led to demand for a referendum on legalizing this practice in another country. Nicolae Ceausescu ("CHOO-sec-oo") enacted a total ban on this practice in Romania in 1966. The health minister Simone Veil names a French law that legalized this practice. Article 9 of the Irish constitution, which banned this practice, was repealed by a 2018 referendum. For 10 points, name this practice in which a woman can elect to not go through with a pregnancy.

Victoria Clark's history of this country takes its title from its leader's quote that leading it is like "dancing on the heads of snakes." Government snipers fired on protesters in Change Square in this country's capital during the Friday of Dignity massacre. An activist from this country founded the organization Women Journalists Without Chains. Along with two Liberian women, (*) Tawakkol Karman won the 2011 Nobel Peace Prize for her role in anti-authoritarian protests in this country. The Security Belt paramilitary reports to the Southern Transitional Council in this country. Abdrabbuh Mansour Hadi became president of this country in 2012 after a deal brokered by the Gulf Cooperation Council. For 10 points, name this country whose Arab Spring protests toppled Ali Abdullah Saleh, who was later killed by its Houthi rebels.

One publication called the Daily [this name] publishes sensational stories about evil spirits called tokoloshe; that publication is the largest daily in South Africa. Ezra Levant called Pierre and Margaret Trudeau "sluts" while host of a show on a Canadian news network of this name derisively called the "Fox News of the North." One publication of this name "on Sunday" replaced (*) News of the World. This is also the name of a publication which printed "Gotcha!" after the General Belgrano was sunk and ascribed to Prime Minister James Callaghan the attitude of "Crisis? What Crisis?" That publication of this name smeared Liverpool fans by accusing them of robbing corpses and pissing on police during the Hillsborough disaster. For 10 points, give this common name of the largest newspaper in Baltimore and the largest British tabloid, an astronomical moniker.
3.r: The Sun [or the Daily Sun; or Sun News Network]

3.q: Pakistani official Jamaat Ali Shah, who oversaw a binational commission concerned with this industry, was forced to flee to Canada after being charged with treason for admitting that this industry may be threatened by climate change rather than secret Hindu conspiracies. The World Bank's Inspector Panel was created after the Morse Commission report prompted the organization to withdraw from a project in this industry in 1993. Narmad Bachao Andolan is dedicated to opposing this industry, which is decried in an essay noting that a project at Bargi has (*) met just 5% of its target output dispute disrupting millions of adivasis. Projects in this industry are analogized to nuclear bombs in the essay "The Greater Common Good," which notes that Nehru called this industry's facilities "the temples of modern India." During a protest against the Sardar Sarovar project in this industry, Arundhati Roy was charged with contempt of court by the Indian Supreme Court. For 10 points, name this industry that has displaced millions of people in the Narmada River valley by building dams.
3.r: hydroelectric industry [or dams before said; prompt on electric industry or power industry or renewables; if someone buzzes in and says “water,” ask “for what purpose?”]
3.c: 2019 Chicago Open Pkt 10 Borglum + Mukherjee Q15

3.q: This man defeated one opponent after that opponent was caught on camera at a McDonalds negotiating with the mother of an underage girl who had been bribed into having an underage sexual relationship. This vanquisher of Buz Lukens won a 2014 primary over J. Winteregg, who claimed this man had "electile dysfunction." This member of the Gang of Seven defeated Roy Blunt to replace Tom (*) Delay and this co-author of No Child Left Behind beat Daniel Webster in a January 2015 election. He faced a July 2015 motion from Mark Meadows to "vacate" his chair due to past apostasies like negotiating the 2011 debt-limit increase and discontent from the Freedom Caucus. For 10 points, identify this man, originally slated to be replaced by Kevin McCarthy, who in 2011 replaced Nancy Pelosi as Speaker of the House.

These people are the subject of a 2006 paper by Susan Rasmussen about their "Moving Beyond the Protest" by using the guitar as a symbol against unemployment. These people developed a one-stringed fiddle that is only played by women whose husbands were sent off to war and which is built by their Inaden caste. Along with the Wodaabe, these people race each other during the Cure Salee festival, where the winner is awarded a broadsword called a takoba. Because these creators of the (*) imzad frequently traverse dangerous terrain near Abalessa, a holy site in the Hoggar Mountains, they are considered some of the best offroad vehicle operators in the world. These speakers of the Tamasheq languages rebelled in 2012 against the government of Amadou Toure to create the state of Azawad. For 10 points, identify this nomadic Berber group in the Sahara known for their characteristic blue tagelmust.
3.c: 2019 Chicago Open Pkt 05 Bollinger + Foster Q11

3.q: A council to recognize figures on this holiday was started and first headed by Olympic middle distance runner Herb Elliot. "Ticket-holder Number 5" and "Toy Town" are short stories in a 2017 collection named after this holiday by Melanie Cheng. Jack Patten and William Ferguson led a march to protest this holiday, calling it a "Day of Mourning", on the same day that a group of indigenous people were forced to run up a beach at Farm Cove to reenact a historical event on this holiday. Awards are given on this holiday to the "Young" person of the year, who have included (*) Ashleigh Barty. Opponents of celebrating this holiday often refer to it as "Invasion Day", since it celebrates the January 26th anniversary of a naval landing by Arthur Philip. For 10 points, identify this holiday that recognizes the First Fleet's arrival in 1788 in a certain country at Sydney Cove.
3.r: Australia Day [or Foundation Day or Anniversary Day; accept Invasion Day before “Invasion”]

3.q: Note to players: specific term required. In a book that raised awareness of this approach, Elizabeth L. Cline linked it to the 2005 expiration of an international quota system called the MFA. The name for this approach was coined in a 1989 New York Times article about a company founded by Spanish billionaire Amancio Ortega. This approach combines the QR style of manufacturing with "dynamic assortment" planning ensuring that the affected industry has fifty-two "microseasons" per year instead of four. The (*) TikTok hashtag #haul fuels the "ultra" form of this business model, which is used by a Singapore-based company that made the most-downloaded shopping app in the U.S. Recent catwalk trends are replicated in, for 10 points, what business model of Zara, Shein, H&M, and other low-cost clothing retailers?
3.r: fast fashion [or ultrafast fashion; prompt on fashion or clothing or textiles before “clothing”]

3.q: A politician from this country who used the slogan "It's my turn" was accused by political opponents of falsifying his age to be younger than 70. A politician in this country sued the makers of the documentary The Lion of Bourdillon. The winner of a recent election in this country had to win at least a quarter of the vote in at least 24 states, which was made harder by the presence of four major candidates including Rabiu Kwankwaso and members from the (*) Peoples Democratic Party and All Progressives Congress. The INEC was criticized by Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi for improperly uploading results after an election in this country once led by Goodluck Jonathan.
